subject: Intermittent fanout instability affecting hosted generation — customer snapshot & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Moore <alex@sunriseai.com>, ops@sunriseai.com
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.inference>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-09-21T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Intermittent fanout instability affecting hosted generation — initial notification

Alex / Sunrise ops team,

We detected an intermittent fanout instability impacting our hosted generation endpoints beginning ~2026-09-21T09:45 PDT. Symptoms: elevated p95/p99 latency for streaming generation requests and a small spike in 502/503 responses for a subset of customers (you may have seen transient "incomplete stream" errors).

Immediate actions taken: 
- Updated our public status page with an incident record (see link below).
- Temporarily disabled prefetch fanout for the affected routing shard to reduce amplification.
- Added a routing rule to prefer dedicated pools for heavy long-sequence requests.
- Increased burst capacity on the US-west pool while we investigate.

What we need from you: if you can, please forward any representative request IDs that saw a 5xx or truncated stream (example: req_12ab34). Those will help us correlate with traces.

Attachments: short diagnostic snippet attached (diagnostic_log_snippet.txt) and a preliminary timeline.

I'll follow up with a technical update in the next 60–90 minutes once we have a root-cause hypothesis. Apologies for the interruption — we know interruptions at peak are disruptive.

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.inference

Status link: https://status.redwood.inference/incident/INC-1234
From: Alex Moore <alex@sunriseai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Cc: ops@sunriseai.com, Lia Chen <lia.chen@sunriseai.com>
Date: 2026-09-21T10:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent fanout instability affecting hosted generation — initial notification

Thanks Marissa — we saw increased tail latency and a few 502s around 09:50–10:05 PDT. Example request IDs we have: req_12ab34, req_12ff78. Impact: a few customer-facing requests timed out and a third-party webhook retry loop was triggered, which caused duplicate downstream work.

Could you confirm whether this is covered under the SLA credit policy for transient 5xx spikes? Also, any ETA on the mitigation being fully in place is helpful.

--
Alex Moore
Head of Platform Ops, Sunrise AI
alex@sunriseai.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.inference>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.inference>
Cc: Alex Moore <alex@sunriseai.com>, ops@sunriseai.com
Date: 2026-09-21T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Intermittent fanout instability — technical interim findings

Marissa / team,

Quick technical summary from the infra side (root-cause hypothesis):
- We observed request amplification in the prefetch fanout codepath. A regression in the contiguous-batcher caused duplicate fanout to peer replicas when a stale KV-sync condition was present. That produced ~1.7x additional downstream requests for certain routing shards under burst loads.
- Amplification coincided with a control-plane state where a subset of nodes reported stale KV cache ages due to a GC spike; the batcher did not coalesce duplicates as expected.

Actions completed: 
1) Disabled prefetch fanout for the affected shards at 11:00 PDT (mitigation).
2) Scaled the US-west dedicated pool by +20% and temporarily routed long-sequence requests to those nodes.
3) Restarted the small set of routing daemons to flush the stale KV state.

Current status: error rates and p99 are trending back toward baseline. We will continue with controlled re-enablement once we validate a fix.

Next steps for postmortem:
- Collect full trace set for amplified requests (Marcus + Sean).
- Identify the batcher regression commit and add a test for the KV-sync edge case.
- Propose a hardening plan for prefetch fanout and a rollout gating checklist.
- Prepare customer-facing root-cause and remedial steps for the postmortem (Marissa to coordinate communications).

I've attached a short CSV timeline (incident_timeline.csv) and a trimmed log snippet showing duplicate outgoing connections.

--
Marcus Lin
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Moore <alex@sunriseai.com>, Lia Chen <lia.chen@sunriseai.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.inference>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-09-21T12:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent fanout instability affecting hosted generation — next steps and customer offer

Alex / Lia,

Thank you for the request IDs — we've correlated req_12ab34 and req_12ff78 to amplified fanout traces and those traces match the pattern Marcus described. The mitigation we applied (disable prefetch on affected shards + routing to dedicated pool) appears to have stabilized the traffic; our p99 has returned to within SLA targets as of 12:05 PDT. We will hold the prefetch disabled until the fix is validated in canary.

Planned follow-up:
- Postmortem will be published to you and the status page by EOD tomorrow (2026-09-22) with timeline, root cause, code fix, and verification plan.
- We will proactively apply a one-time usage credit for affected requests equivalent to the token charges for the window 09:45–11:15 PDT; formal credit details will be included in the postmortem.

If you'd like an interim 1:1 to go over traces and mitigations, I can set up a 30-minute call this afternoon; otherwise we'll share the full report tomorrow.

Thanks again for the quick heads-up and for sharing the request IDs — that sped up correlation.

Regards,
--
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.inference
From: Alex Moore <alex@sunriseai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-09-21T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent fanout instability affecting hosted generation — acknowledgment

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the quick detection, mitigation, and the offer of credit. A short call would be helpful to review the traces; 15:30 PDT works for our team.

--
Alex
